title: ModTheSpire2
description:
ModTheSpire2 is a pre-launch mod selector and restart helper for Slay the Spire 2.

GitHub:
https://github.com/grassdog0/MTS2

Main features:
- Windows launcher with no extra runtime install.
- Choose vanilla, selected mods, load order, and named profiles before the game starts.
- Launcher default view now reads the current game settings.save order and enabled state, improving compatibility with RitsuLib, Better Mod Menu, and the base game's own mod manager.
- Named profiles apply immediately when selected; the old extra Load Profile button has been removed.
- Dependencies are still shown with visual indentation when possible, without rewriting the current settings.save order just to display a tree.
- Dependency-aware Windows mod list and compatibility with common Workshop manifest layouts.
- In-game Close and Open Launcher button for changing whole-mod enablement safely.
- Close and Open Launcher forwards the current game command line, so renderer flags such as --rendering-driver opengl3 are preserved.
- Steam launch option remains:
"<path to ModTheSpire2Launcher.exe>" -- %command%
- Put extra game arguments after %command%.

Experimental cross-platform preview:
- Added ModTheSpire2Launcher.sh for native Linux / Steam Deck.
- Added ModTheSpire2Launcher.command for native macOS Steam.
- These Linux/macOS launchers are lightweight script-menu previews, not full GUI launchers.
- Linux/macOS support has not been verified on real systems yet. Volunteers and feedback are needed.

Workshop cannot edit Steam launch options automatically. If you want Steam Play to open ModTheSpire2 first, set the launch option manually.
changeNote:
Launcher compatibility update
- Windows launcher now opens from the current settings.save order and enabled state by default.
- This improves compatibility with RitsuLib, Better Mod Menu, and other tools that manage mod order.
- Named profiles now apply immediately from the profile dropdown.
- Removed the redundant Load Profile button.
- Dependency indentation is preserved visually without reordering the current settings.save list just for display.
- Existing launch option, renderer-argument forwarding, and Linux/macOS preview scripts remain included.
